A fix for Go functions that redeploy when nothing in them changed. Still built on upstream [v4.17.2](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/releases/tag/v4.17.2).

### Fixes

- **A Go function no longer changes when only the git commit changes.** Go wrote the git revision and commit time into every binary it built, so a new commit gave a new binary and a new zip even if no Go file changed, and the next `sst deploy` uploaded new code for every Go function in the project. Deploy builds now pass `-buildvcs=false`, and so do the release builds of the `sst dev` bridge task image. The first deploy after you update uploads each Go function once, because the binary changes; after that, a commit alone leaves them as they are. On a real Go function, an empty commit and a second deploy updated it before the fix and left it alone after. Dev builds are unchanged. ([#109](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/109), [anomalyco/sst#6976](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6976))

### Also

- The `Run` resource no longer hangs on a command that prints a line longer than 64 KB, and it reads stdout and stderr together, so a command that writes a lot to stderr can't block either. A line over 1 MB is replaced by a note and the lines after it still come through. Nothing in SST 4 creates a `Run` resource today, so no config reaches this yet. ([#110](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/110), [anomalyco/sst#7006](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/7006))

### Docs

- The PlanetScale guide explains `successor` on `PostgresBranchRole`, which a role that owns objects needs before SST can remove it, and the Postgres examples set it. ([#111](https://github.com/sst-community/sst/pull/111), [anomalyco/sst#6932](https://github.com/anomalyco/sst/pull/6932))

### Install

```bash
npm install sst@npm:@sst-community/sst@4.21.1
```

To switch an existing project:

1. Check that `node --version` shows `v22` or later, wherever you run `sst`, CI included.
2. Set its dependency to `"sst": "npm:@sst-community/sst@4.21.1"` and reinstall.

For a project that isn't JavaScript, install the CLI globally. It still needs Node.js 22 or later, to run `sst.config.ts`:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sst-community/sst/main/install | bash
```
